body: My concern with being this explicit is that some users will take it literally and call `new()` without arguments for constructors that do require arguments.

I myself feel like `Make an instance using "var %s = %s.new()"` is technically misleading. You make the instance with `new()`, _then_ assign it to a newly declared variable.
The solution provided in the error should at least imply this is just an _example_ on how to possibly solve this.

I suppose we can add `...` between the parentheses to denote that arguments that may be required. However, none of the built-in Godot classes require a parameter for `new()`, so maybe we can detect this and append the `...` conditionally.

Also, this warning doesn't work correctly for unnamed classes, suggesting invalid syntax (`Make an instance using "var res://node.gd = res://node.gd.new()"`). I think we should just add a static example like `SomeClass.new()` rather than trying to implement smart hints, as that requires more effort than it looks.
